The negotiated speed matches the selecte: The negotiated speed matches the selected polling mode, so the normalized values below describe that mode.
Delivery timing begins when firmware rec: Delivery timing begins when firmware receives a keyboard report and ends on the keyboard USB IN completion, including queue wait. The minimum is this connection’s fixed offset between the firmware tick and the USB frame; it is re-drawn on every replug, so compare runs by Maximum minus Minimum rather than by the absolute values.
Quantiles are bounded estimates from eig: Quantiles are bounded estimates from eight fixed histogram buckets, not raw-sample percentiles.
This separates long firmware main-loop g: This separates long firmware main-loop gaps from HID delivery timing.
These are the values captured at the end: These are the values captured at the end of this test, not a live reading — they only change when a test produces a new snapshot. Applying a polling mode restarts the keyboard, which zeroes them, so a test run right after a mode change always starts near zero. To check whether an unplug, suspend or speed change was counted, trigger it and then run another short test.

Rows marked “speed mismatch” enumerated: Rows marked “speed mismatch” enumerated at a USB speed the selected mode cannot run at, so their normalized columns (p99 bound, > 2×) are not comparable with the other rows.
Compare runs with <1>Spread</1>, Drops a: Compare runs with <1>Spread</1>, Drops and Queue. Avg and Max each carry a constant offset that is fixed when the keyboard enumerates and is re-drawn on every replug, so the same firmware in the same mode can report very different microseconds between runs. Spread (Max minus Min, in polling intervals) removes that offset and shows how many extra intervals reports had to wait. The p99 and > 2× columns are measured against each mode’s own interval, so they answer “did this mode stay inside its own budget?” rather than which mode is faster.
